name: Unica workbook page recipes
note: Follows Cedric's decisions up to Nov 2, 2026. Where the curriculum spreadsheet's 'Workbook format' tab disagrees (fixed second unit B every day, parent line on the cover, level map on the back, parent-supported U4-U6), these recipes win.

page.answer_boxes: right-aligned to the column edge, one x position per column

header.name_and_date: only on the first page of each day
header.day_line: Day N · Page n of P
header.instruction_line: always one line under the title

workbook.spare_pages: extra_practice pages from this workbook's steps, never blank

cover.subtitle_pattern: <Name> will <what they will learn, one sentence>

how_page.stuck: Ask for help using Maya, the AI Teaching Assistant.
how_page.fix_it: Anything your child got wrong in the previous workbook comes back as new questions.

workbook.back_matter: none (no My levels page; that lives in the app)

progression.rule: Each workbook follows the natural order of the level's skills and their steps. Every day moves on: new pages start at the next step, or the next skill once a skill's steps are done. Day 10 is clearly harder than Day 1.
progression.numbers: pick in code from the step's numbers ranges; easy items from the lower part of the range, hard items from the upper part
progression.questions: fill the step's templates (practice questions are models, not copies); a page's questions all belong to its step
progression.review: spaced: a step passed at 90% comes back after about 2 days, 1 week, 3 weeks and 2 months
progression.challenge: from the hardest step reached so far that day, never easier than the practice pages
progression.fallback: If today's step has no template of a page's required format (for example no story template for a Number stories page), take that page's items from the latest earlier step of the same skill that has one, then from the previous skill. Never from a later step.
progression.how_do_you_know: A 'How do you know?' item is a story item with one extra line under it: 'How do you know? ____'. The generator adds it; it needs no explain template.

with.title: Friday 5
with.instruction: Five questions from the last few weeks. No hints.
with.questions_from: the last three weeks of work

with.title: Show what you know
with.instruction: Ten days of work. Show what you learned!
with.questions_from: one item from each step this workbook, and the hardest ones again

with.title: Math in the world
with.instruction: Plan it, solve it, and explain your answer.
with.questions_from: one multi-step real task using this workbook's steps

fill_rules: If more than 15% of the question area is empty, add one more item from the same step (up to the page's max) and lay out again.
If still more than 15% empty, spread the space evenly between items (up to 48 px extra per gap), never all at the bottom.
If items overflow, move the last item to the next page of the same type, or drop it if it is a duplicate.
variety_rules: No sentence frame twice on one page, and at most twice in a day.
At least min_formats_on_page different formats per page.
Never the same item twice in a workbook.
True/false items: about half true, half false across a page.

notation.pictures: (picture: ...) is an art instruction, never printed as text
